title: Frustum culling for instanced meshes
purpose: Read the six frustum planes from a column-major view-projection matrix, classify spheres and boxes as outside, intersecting or inside, and compact the visible instance matrices of a three.js InstancedMesh so only they are drawn, with WebGL or WebGPU depth. Use it for large forests, crowds and city blocks.

engine.name: node
engine.notes: No three.js needed: matrices are plain or typed arrays (Matrix4.elements works). The demo was rendered with three.js 0.186.1 in headless Chrome.

exports.name: frustumPlanes
exports.summary: Normalized planes [a, b, c, d] left, right, bottom, top, near, far; inside where a x + b y + c z + d >= 0.

exports.name: classifySphere
exports.summary: OUTSIDE, INTERSECTS or INSIDE for a sphere.

exports.name: classifyBox
exports.summary: OUTSIDE, INTERSECTS or INSIDE for an axis-aligned box (conservative near frustum corners).

exports.name: cullInstances
exports.signature: cullInstances(source, radius, planes, target, options = {}) -> count
exports.summary: Copy the visible instance matrices to the front of target in order and return how many; in place allowed.

exports.name: multiplyMatrices
exports.summary: Column-major product a * b, for projection * view (* model).

exports.name: FRUSTUM_CULL_DEFAULTS
exports.summary: Frozen default options: depthZeroToOne, center, indices.

options.name: depthZeroToOne
options.meaning: frustumPlanes: clip z in [0, w] (WebGPU) instead of [-w, w] (WebGL).

options.name: center
options.meaning: cullInstances: bounding sphere centre in the model's space.

options.name: indices
options.meaning: cullInstances: receives the kept instance numbers.

limits: Bounding spheres only for instances: a long thin model gets a loose sphere and is kept more often than needed. Plane tests are conservative near frustum corners, where a box or sphere just outside two planes counts as intersecting. No occlusion culling and no level of detail. Culling runs on the CPU every time you call it, in O(instances); for very large counts a GPU pass or a spatial hierarchy is faster. Compacting in place loses the culled matrices, so keep a full copy to cull again next frame. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run for the demo, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Gribb and Hartmann plane extraction from the view-projection matrix
Signed distance of a bounding sphere to normalized planes
Positive and negative vertex test for axis-aligned boxes
